title: Mapping property of a normalized blowup for arbitrary normal sources
statement: Let $S$ be a reduced scheme of finite type over $\mathbf Q$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $J\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ be a coherent quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent] such that $S\setminus V(J)$ is dense in every irreducible component. Put $N=(\operatorname{Bl}_J(S))^\nu$ and let $p:N\to S$ be the normalized-blowup map [def-trf-normalized-blowup]. Then $N$ is normal, meaning its local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $p$ takes generic points to generic points [def-sc-generic-point], and the extended ideal $J\mathcal O_N$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] is an invertible ideal, meaning an ideal locally generated by a nonzerodivisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. For every normal scheme $Y$ and morphism $f:Y\to S$ taking generic points of irreducible components to generic points, if $J\mathcal O_Y$ is an invertible ideal, there is a unique $S$-morphism $Y\to N$. There is no quasi-compactness, local Noetherianity, or finite-type assumption on $Y$.

source.place: ILO Expose VIII 2.2.2 and Proposition 2.2.4(i), printed p.90; universal-property input of lem-trf-local-term-locality proof (1)--(2). Stacks Tags 0806 (divisors.tex, lemma-universal-property-blowing-up) and 035Q(4) (morphisms.tex, lemma-normalization-normal).

proof.text:
Put $U=S\setminus V(J)$ and $B=\operatorname{Bl}_J(S)$, with map $b:B	o S$. By lem-trf-reduced-blowup-generic-geometry, $B$ is reduced and locally Noetherian with finitely many irreducible components, $b^{-1}U	o U$ is an isomorphism, and $b$ bijects generic points. By def-trf-normalized-blowup, $N=B^
u$ and $p=b\circ
u_B$. Apply lem-sfb-componentwise-normalization-generic-properties to $B$: $N$ is normal and $
u_B$ takes generic points to generic points. Composing with $b$ proves the generic-point assertion for $p$.

proof.text: By thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center, $J\mathcal O_B$ is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor. Refine that cover to affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ on which $J\mathcal O_B=(a)$ with $a$ regular. By lem-sfb-normalization-affine-total-fractions, $\nu_B^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}\overline A$, where $\overline A\subset Q(A)$ is the integral closure of $A$ in its total fraction ring. The element $a$ is a unit in $Q(A)$, so multiplication by $a$ is injective on its subring $\overline A$. The extended ideal on this inverse image is $(a)\overline A$: extension is generated by the images of the generators, and applying two ring maps successively gives the same generated ideal as their composite. Thus $J\mathcal O_N$ is generated by a nonzerodivisor on this cover, exactly the effective Cartier ideal condition of def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal. This proves the invertibility assertion without assuming that normalization is flat.

proof.text: Let $Y,f$ satisfy the stated hypotheses. Apply thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property to the canonical invertible extended ideal $J\mathcal O_Y$: there is a unique $g:Y\to B$ with $b\circ g=f$. This is the final-object clause of that theorem, with the quotient whose image is the extended ideal, rather than an arbitrarily chosen quotient. We check component dominance for this particular $g$. If $\eta$ is the generic point of an irreducible component of $Y$, then $f(\eta)$ is a generic point of $S$, hence lies in $U$. The isomorphism $b^{-1}U\to U$ and the generic-point bijection of lem-trf-reduced-blowup-generic-geometry force $g(\eta)$ to be the corresponding generic point of $B$. For the component $C=\overline{\{\eta\}}$, continuity gives $g(C)\subset\overline{\{g(\eta)\}}$, and $g(\eta)\in g(C)$ gives the reverse inclusion after closure. Therefore $C$ dominates that irreducible component of $B$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 2.2.1--2.2.4(i), printed p.90 (PDF p.96); Stacks divisors.tex Tags 0806, 02OS and morphisms.tex Tags 035P, 035Q, 0CDV.

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-component-dominant-normalization-lift to $g:Y\to B$. Its target condition holds because $B$ has finitely many irreducible components, so every quasi-compact open has finitely many components; the nonempty intersections with the finitely many components of $B$ give all components of the open. Its source condition is exactly the assumed normality of $Y$, and component dominance was checked in step 3. It gives a unique $h:Y\to B^\nu=N$ with $\nu_B\circ h=g$. Then $p\circ h=b\circ g=f$, proving existence. The cited lift theorem imposes no quasi-compactness, local Noetherianity or finite-type condition on $Y$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 2.2.1--2.2.4(i), printed p.90 (PDF p.96); Stacks divisors.tex Tags 0806, 02OS and morphisms.tex Tags 035P, 035Q, 0CDV.

proof.text: If $h_1,h_2:Y\to N$ are $S$-morphisms, both $\nu_B\circ h_i$ lie over $f$. The final-object clause of thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property identifies both with the unique $g$ of step 3. The uniqueness clause of lem-sfb-component-dominant-normalization-lift, applied to that same $g$, now gives $h_1=h_2$. This also covers $Y=\varnothing$. If $S=\varnothing$, its blowup and normalization are empty and any $Y\to S$ has empty source; the same argument applies. For $J=\mathcal O_S$ it reduces to the normalization mapping property.

The statement and stmt_deps are identical to the node Q15 created, and the item is still unsplit live with no re-split note. ILO VIII 2.2.1-2.2.4(i) (printed p.90) proves the item by combining the universal properties of blow-ups and normalizations, and the split writes that combination out. Step 1: B is reduced and locally Noetherian with finitely many components, per lem-trf-reduced-blowup-generic-geometry. lem-sfb-componentwise-normalization-generic-properties then gives normality of N and the generic-point claim. Step 2: J O_B is locally (a) with a a nonzerodivisor (principalizes-center). By the total-fractions node the inverse image is Spec of Abar inside Q(A), and a is a unit of Q(A), so a is a nonzerodivisor on Abar. The extended ideal is transitive by right exactness. This is elementary and correct. Step 3: the blow-up final-object property (blueprint_update, no conditions on Y) gives a unique g. Density puts every generic point of S in U, injectivity of b on the inverse image of U gives g(eta) = xi, and so each component of Y dominates a component of B. Step 4: lem-sfb-component-dominant-normalization-lift (035Q(4)) applies because B has finitely many components and Y is normal. Step 5: uniqueness of g, then uniqueness of the lift. Edge cases checked: J = O_S, J = 0 excluded by density, empty schemes, two lines meeting with J the origin's ideal, non-Noetherian Y. Acyclic; proof_deps equal the union of the steps' uses; no SGA; the 3 sfb generic tool_uses are accepted and the 2 nagata nodes are Lean-closed.
